text: Which of the following is an example of the BPO (Business Process Outsourcing) sector of the IT-ITeS industry?
options: A company writing operating system software
A call centre handling customer support for a bank
explanation: BPO refers to outsourcing non-core business processes such as customer support/call centre work to a third-party service provider.

text: Which segment of the IT-ITeS industry deals with designing, developing and maintaining computer software?
explanation: The IT Services and Software Products segment covers software design, development, testing and maintenance.

text: KPO stands for:
explanation: KPO (Knowledge Process Outsourcing) involves outsourcing knowledge-intensive, domain-specific work such as research and analytics.

text: Which of the following is a soft skill useful for a career in the IT-ITeS industry?
explanation: Soft skills like communication, teamwork and time management are personal attributes valued alongside technical skills in the IT-ITeS industry.

text: A person working in a data centre monitoring servers and network equipment is most likely employed in which sector?
explanation: Data centre operations and server/network monitoring are core activities of the IT-ITeS industry.

text: Which of the following best describes 'ITeS'?
options: IT-enabled Services delivered using IT infrastructure and telecom networks
explanation: ITeS (IT-enabled Services) refers to services delivered over IT and telecom infrastructure, such as BPO and call centres.

text: Which of these job roles belongs to the IT-ITeS industry?
explanation: A Data Entry Operator inputs and manages digital data, a core role within the IT-ITeS industry.

text: The IT-ITeS industry in India is a major contributor to:
explanation: The IT-ITeS industry significantly contributes to India's export earnings, GDP and large-scale employment generation.

text: Which of the following is NOT typically considered part of the IT-ITeS industry?
explanation: Traditional handloom weaving is a craft/textile activity, not part of the IT (software) or ITeS (IT-enabled services) industry.

text: 'Domain knowledge' in the context of the IT-ITeS industry refers to:
options: Knowledge of internet domain names only
Specialised knowledge about a particular field or industry an employee works in
Knowledge of a computer's IP address
explanation: Domain knowledge means understanding the specific business area (e.g. banking, healthcare) in which IT/ITeS services are being applied.

text: In touch typing, which row of keys is called the 'home row'?
options: The row with function keys F1-F12
explanation: The home row (ASDFGHJKL;) is where the fingers rest by default, and other keys are reached from this position.

text: Which finger is conventionally used to press the Spacebar while touch typing?
explanation: In standard touch typing technique, either thumb is used to press the Spacebar.

text: What is the primary goal of learning touch typing?
options: To type using only two fingers
To increase typing speed and accuracy without looking at the keyboard
To memorise the mouse pointer position
To reduce the number of keys on the keyboard
explanation: Touch typing trains a person to type quickly and accurately from muscle memory, without looking at the keys.

text: Which key is used to move the cursor to a new line and paragraph while typing text?
explanation: The Enter key inserts a paragraph/line break, moving the cursor to a new line.

text: Typing speed is generally measured in:
explanation: Typing speed is conventionally measured in words per minute (WPM), based on standard word length of 5 characters.

text: Which of the following is a benefit of accurate data entry?
options: It reduces errors in stored records and improves data reliability
It increases the need for retyping
It has no effect on data quality
explanation: Accurate data entry reduces mistakes in records, improving the reliability and usability of stored data.

text: The Caps Lock key, when active, primarily affects:
options: The case (upper/lower) of alphabet keys typed
explanation: Caps Lock toggles the alphabetic keys to type in uppercase (capital letters) until turned off.

text: Which posture guideline is recommended for correct ergonomics while doing data entry work?
options: Slouching with wrists bent upward on the desk edge
Sitting upright with feet flat on the floor and wrists straight
Keeping the monitor at floor level
explanation: Correct ergonomic posture — upright sitting, feet flat, wrists straight/neutral — reduces strain and injury risk during prolonged typing.

text: In the QWERTY keyboard layout, which key lies immediately to the left of the 'A' key?
explanation: On a standard QWERTY keyboard, the Caps Lock key is positioned immediately to the left of the 'A' key.

text: Why is regular practice important for improving keyboarding skills?
options: It has no impact on speed or accuracy
It builds muscle memory, increasing speed and reducing errors over time
It only helps with mouse usage
It is required only for gaming
explanation: Consistent practice reinforces correct finger movements, building muscle memory that improves both typing speed and accuracy.

text: Which LibreOffice Writer feature is used to combine a form letter with a list of names and addresses to produce personalised letters?
explanation: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source to generate multiple personalised copies of a document.

text: In LibreOffice Writer, which menu contains the 'Track Changes' option?
explanation: Track Changes is accessed from Edit > Track Changes in LibreOffice Writer.

text: What is the purpose of the Track Changes feature in a word processor?
options: To record insertions, deletions and formatting changes made by reviewers for later acceptance or rejection
To compress the document file size
explanation: Track Changes marks edits made to a document so that the original author can review and accept or reject each change.

text: Which file format is the default native format for documents saved in LibreOffice Writer?
explanation: LibreOffice Writer's native/default format is the OpenDocument Text format, with extension .odt.

text: Which feature automatically generates a list of headings along with their page numbers at the beginning of a long document?
explanation: The Table of Contents feature scans heading styles used in the document and compiles them with page numbers into a navigable list.

text: In a word processor, a 'style' is best described as:
options: A single colour applied to text
A predefined set of formatting attributes (font, size, spacing, etc.) that can be applied consistently
explanation: A style bundles formatting attributes together so they can be applied uniformly and updated in one place across a document.

text: Which option in LibreOffice Writer allows a note to be added to explain or comment on a portion of text without altering the text itself?
explanation: The Comment feature attaches an annotation to selected text, visible in the margin, without changing the document's actual content.

text: Which term refers to text/graphics that repeats at the top of every page of a document?
explanation: A header is content, such as a title or page number, that repeats at the top margin of each page.

text: Which feature in a word processor is used to search for a specific word and substitute it with another word throughout the document?
explanation: Find & Replace locates occurrences of a search term and replaces them with a specified replacement text.

text: In LibreOffice Writer, which shortcut key is commonly used to open the Find & Replace dialog box?
explanation: Ctrl+H opens the Find & Replace dialog box in LibreOffice Writer.

text: What does the term 'orphan control' relate to in word processing?
options: Preventing a single line of a paragraph from being left alone at the bottom of a page
Protecting a document with a password
explanation: Orphan control prevents the first line of a paragraph from being isolated at the bottom of a page, separated from the rest of the paragraph.

text: Which feature lets a user protect a document so that it can only be opened by entering a password?
explanation: When saving a document, LibreOffice Writer offers an option to set a password so only authorised users can open it.

text: In the context of mail merge, the file containing variable data such as names and addresses for each recipient is called the:
explanation: The data source holds the variable information (like names and addresses) that gets merged into the main document for each recipient.

text: Which of the following best describes a 'template' in Writer?
options: A predesigned document layout used as a starting point for creating new documents with consistent formatting
explanation: A template provides preset formatting, styles and layout that can be reused as the basis for new documents.

text: Which feature automatically corrects common typing mistakes, such as 'teh' to 'the', as you type?
explanation: AutoCorrect automatically fixes recognised typing errors and applies predefined replacements while typing.

text: Which of the following is used to insert a numbered reference at the bottom of the same page to provide additional information about a term?
explanation: A footnote places a numbered explanatory note at the bottom of the page, linked to a marker in the main text.

text: In LibreOffice Writer, which view/feature helps to check a document for spelling and grammar errors?
explanation: The Spelling and Grammar tool, typically launched with the F7 key, scans the document and highlights possible spelling/grammar errors.

text: What is the effect of inserting a 'page break' in a document?
options: It ends the current page and forces subsequent content to start on a new page
It deletes all text after the cursor
It changes the font of the whole document
It merges two paragraphs into one
explanation: A page break forces the content following it to start at the top of the next page, regardless of how much space remains on the current page.

text: Which formatting option is used to arrange document text into two or more vertical sections on a page, as seen in newsletters?
explanation: The Columns feature divides the page into multiple side-by-side vertical text blocks, commonly used in newsletters.

text: In LibreOffice Writer, which shortcut is used to make selected text bold?
explanation: Ctrl+B applies or removes bold formatting on the selected text.

text: Which feature allows a specific piece of text or location to be marked so it can be quickly navigated to later?
explanation: A bookmark marks a position or selection in a document so the user can jump back to it quickly using Insert > Bookmark and navigation tools.

text: Which of these is an example of a paragraph alignment option in a word processor?
explanation: Justify is a paragraph alignment option that stretches text so both left and right margins are evenly aligned; the others are character formatting options.

text: The process of combining two or more selected table cells into a single cell in Writer is called:
explanation: Merge Cells combines the content and space of two or more adjacent selected table cells into a single cell.

text: Which of the following is the correct sequence of steps to start a Mail Merge in LibreOffice Writer using the Mail Merge Wizard?
options: Tools > Mail Merge Wizard, then select/create data source and main document, then merge
explanation: In LibreOffice Writer, the Mail Merge Wizard is launched from Tools > Mail Merge Wizard, which then guides through selecting the data source, editing the document and completing the merge.

text: Which term describes text that is set to appear slightly above the normal line, such as in x²?
explanation: Superscript formatting raises characters slightly above the baseline, commonly used for exponents like x².

text: Which function in LibreOffice Calc returns the sum of values in a range of cells?
explanation: The SUM function adds up all numeric values in the specified range, e.g. =SUM(A1:A10).

text: Which spreadsheet function returns the arithmetic mean of a range of numeric cells?
explanation: AVERAGE calculates the mean by adding the numeric values in the range and dividing by the count of those values.

text: In LibreOffice Calc, which symbol must precede a formula for it to be evaluated as a calculation rather than treated as text?
explanation: Every formula in Calc begins with an equal sign (=), which tells the program to compute rather than display the entry as plain text.

text: What does the cell reference $A$1 represent in a formula?
options: A relative reference that changes on copying
An absolute reference that stays fixed to column A, row 1 when the formula is copied
explanation: The dollar signs before both the column letter and row number lock the reference, so it does not change when the formula is copied elsewhere.

text: Which function returns the largest value among a set of numbers in a range?
explanation: The MAX function scans the given range and returns the highest numeric value found.

text: Which function returns the smallest value among a set of numbers in a range?
explanation: The MIN function scans the given range and returns the lowest numeric value found.

text: Which function counts only the cells containing numeric values in a specified range?
explanation: COUNT counts the number of cells in a range that contain numeric data, ignoring text and blank cells.

text: Which function would you use to count the number of non-empty cells, whether they contain text or numbers, in a range?
explanation: COUNTA counts all non-empty cells in a range regardless of whether they contain text, numbers or other data.

text: What is the correct syntax for the IF function in LibreOffice Calc?
explanation: The IF function takes a logical condition first, followed by the value to return if true and the value to return if false: =IF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false).

text: Which function is used to look up a value in the first column of a range and return a value from a specified column in the same row?
explanation: VLOOKUP searches vertically down the first column of a range for a match and returns a value from a specified column index in that row.

text: Which function is used to look up a value along the first row of a range and return a value from a specified row in the same column?
explanation: HLOOKUP searches horizontally across the first row of a range for a match and returns a value from a specified row in that column.

text: Which function adds up only the values in a range that satisfy a given condition?
explanation: SUMIF sums the values in a range for which a specified condition is true, e.g. =SUMIF(A1:A10,">50").

text: Which chart type is most suitable for showing the proportion of each category as a percentage of a whole?
explanation: A pie chart divides a circle into slices, each representing a category's proportion of the total, making it suitable for showing percentage shares.

text: In LibreOffice Calc, freezing rows and columns is used to:
options: Keep specific rows/columns visible on screen while scrolling through the rest of the sheet
explanation: Freeze Rows and Columns keeps selected header rows/columns fixed in view while the rest of the worksheet scrolls, aiding readability of large sheets.

text: What is the term for a group of related worksheets stored together in a single spreadsheet file?
explanation: A workbook is the spreadsheet file itself, which can contain one or more individual worksheets (sheets).

text: Which feature in LibreOffice Calc summarises, groups and analyses large amounts of data interactively, allowing quick reorganisation of rows and columns?
explanation: A Pivot Table lets users summarise and analyse large datasets by dragging fields into rows, columns and values to view aggregated results interactively.

text: Which feature automatically changes the appearance (e.g. colour) of a cell based on whether its value meets a specified condition?
explanation: Conditional Formatting applies formatting such as colour or icons to cells automatically when their content meets specified rules.

text: Which feature restricts the type or range of data that can be entered into a cell, such as allowing only whole numbers between 1 and 100?
explanation: Data Validation lets the user set rules that control what values are acceptable in a cell, preventing invalid entries.

text: In cell referencing, what does a 'mixed reference' such as A$1 or $A1 indicate?
options: Both row and column are locked
Neither row nor column is locked
Only one of the row or column is locked while the other remains relative
The reference points to another workbook
explanation: A mixed reference locks either the row or the column (with a $ sign) while leaving the other part relative, so only one part stays fixed on copying.

text: Which feature lets you quickly fill a series of numbers, dates, or a repeating pattern into adjacent cells by dragging the fill handle?
explanation: AutoFill extends a pattern or series (like 1,2,3 or dates) into adjacent cells by dragging the small fill handle at the corner of a selection.

text: Which of the following correctly represents a cell range from cell B2 to cell D5 in a formula?
explanation: In spreadsheet formulas, a colon (:) is used to denote a continuous range of cells, so B2:D5 refers to the rectangular block from B2 to D5.

text: Which function would correctly calculate the number of days between two dates stored in cells A1 (earlier date) and B1 (later date)?
explanation: Subtracting an earlier date from a later date (=B1-A1) gives the number of days between them, since dates are stored internally as serial numbers.

text: What does the term 'What-If Analysis' generally refer to in a spreadsheet?
options: Exploring how changing input values affects the results of formulas, e.g. using Goal Seek
Protecting a worksheet with a password
explanation: What-If Analysis tools, such as Goal Seek, let users see how changing certain input values changes calculated outcomes in the spreadsheet.

text: Which of the following is the correct order of operator precedence (highest to lowest) generally followed in spreadsheet formulas?
explanation: Spreadsheet formulas follow standard mathematical precedence: expressions in parentheses first, then exponentiation, then multiplication/division, then addition/subtraction.

text: Which function is best used to count the number of cells in a range that meet a specific condition, such as cells greater than 50?
explanation: COUNTIF counts the cells in a range that satisfy a given condition, e.g. =COUNTIF(A1:A10,">50").

text: Which LibreOffice application is used to create slide-based presentations?
explanation: LibreOffice Impress is the dedicated application for creating and editing slide-based presentations.

text: Which feature in Impress controls the common layout, background and placeholder formatting shared across all slides in a presentation?
explanation: The Slide Master defines the default design elements (background, fonts, placeholders) that are inherited by all slides using that master.

text: What is a 'slide transition' in a presentation?
options: The animation effect applied to text within a slide
The visual effect that occurs when moving from one slide to the next during a slide show
A file format for saving presentations
explanation: A slide transition is the visual effect (like fade or wipe) that plays as the presentation moves from one slide to the next.

text: What is a 'custom animation' in Impress used for?
options: Changing the effect applied when switching between slides
Applying motion effects to individual objects or text within a single slide
Changing the file format of the presentation
explanation: Custom animation applies effects like entrance, emphasis or exit to specific objects/text placed on a slide, rather than to the transition between slides.

text: Which Impress view arranges thumbnails of all slides together, making it easy to rearrange, delete, or duplicate slides?
explanation: Slide Sorter view shows small thumbnails of every slide in the deck, allowing quick reordering, deletion, and duplication.

text: Which view in Impress lets a presenter type and edit private reminders or additional information for each slide, not shown to the audience?
explanation: Notes view allows the presenter to add speaker notes attached to each slide, visible only to the presenter and not projected to the audience.

text: In Impress, what is a 'placeholder'?
options: A predefined empty box on a slide layout meant to hold specific content like a title, text, or image
explanation: A placeholder is a container built into a slide's layout, marked for specific content types (title, text, image, etc.), ready to be filled in.

text: Which file extension is the default native format used when saving a presentation in LibreOffice Impress?
explanation: LibreOffice Impress's native OpenDocument format for presentations uses the extension .odp.

text: Which feature in Impress allows a presentation to advance automatically from one slide to the next after a specified time, without manual clicks?
options: Automatic slide timing (advance slide after set duration)
explanation: Setting automatic slide timing under transitions lets slides advance on their own after a chosen number of seconds, rather than waiting for a mouse click.

text: Which Impress view displays only the text content of slides (titles and bullet points) in an indented list, without graphics?
explanation: Outline view shows the textual content of all slides as a structured, indented list, hiding images and other graphical elements for quick text editing.

text: What is the primary purpose of using a consistent design template across a presentation?
options: To maintain a uniform, professional look with consistent fonts, colours and layout throughout the presentation
explanation: A consistent design template ensures visual uniformity (fonts, colour scheme, layout) across all slides, giving the presentation a professional appearance.

text: Which of the following is an example of an 'entrance' animation effect in Impress?
options: None of these are entrance effects
explanation: Fade In is an entrance effect, making an object gradually appear on the slide; Fade Out and Spin exit are typically exit-type effects.

text: In Impress, what does 'Rehearse Timings' allow a presenter to do?
options: Practice the presentation while Impress records the time spent on each slide, for use in automatic timing
explanation: Rehearse Timings runs the slide show while recording how long the presenter spends on each slide, which can then be saved as automatic slide timings.

text: Which of the following is best suited for printing multiple small slide images per page, often used to give the audience a paper reference?
explanation: Handouts print several slide thumbnails on one page, commonly distributed to an audience as a reference during or after a presentation.

text: Which term describes inserting an object such as a chart or image linked to or embedded within a slide?
explanation: Embedding (or inserting) an object places a chart, image or other content directly into a slide, either linked to its source or fully embedded.

text: Which Impress feature is used to add hyperlinks that jump to another slide, a website, or an external file when clicked during a slide show?
explanation: The Hyperlink (or Interaction) feature lets an object or text be linked so that clicking it during the show navigates to another slide, file, or URL.

text: What is the recommended practice regarding the amount of text placed on a single presentation slide?
options: Fill the entire slide with dense paragraphs of text
Keep text concise, using brief bullet points, to maintain audience attention and readability
Avoid using any text at all
Use the smallest possible font size to fit more text
explanation: Good presentation design favours concise bullet points over dense text, keeping slides readable and helping retain audience attention.

text: Which of the following file formats can typically be used to export a LibreOffice Impress presentation for universal viewing without needing presentation software?
options: It cannot be exported to any other format
explanation: Impress can export a presentation to PDF, which preserves the slide layout and can be viewed on almost any device without presentation software.

text: Which term refers to running the presentation in full-screen mode, displaying one slide at a time to an audience?
explanation: Starting the Slide Show (commonly with the F5 key) displays the presentation full-screen, one slide at a time, in sequence.

text: Which of the following is a guideline for effective use of colour and contrast on presentation slides?
options: Use low-contrast text and background colours that are hard to distinguish
Use sufficient contrast between text and background colours so text remains easily readable
Use a different random colour scheme on every slide
Avoid using any background colour or theme
explanation: Good design practice recommends strong contrast between text and background colours to ensure the text is legible to the audience.

text: Which of the following is an example of verbal communication?
options: Sending a text message to a friend
explanation: Verbal communication uses words, whether spoken or written; a text message uses written words, so it is verbal. Nodding, frowning and posture are forms of non-verbal (body language) communication.

text: In the communication cycle, the person who receives and interprets the message is called the
explanation: The receiver is the person to whom the message is directed; they decode the message sent by the sender through a chosen channel.

text: Which of these is an example of a barrier to effective communication?
options: Loud background noise during a conversation
Giving the listener your full attention
explanation: Physical noise in the environment can distort or block a message, making it a common barrier to effective communication.

text: Maintaining eye contact and using appropriate facial expressions while speaking are examples of
explanation: Eye contact and facial expressions are forms of body language, which fall under non-verbal communication.

text: 'Feedback' in the communication cycle refers to
options: The medium used to send a message
The receiver's response that tells the sender how the message was understood
The original idea in the sender's mind
explanation: Feedback is the receiver's reaction or response, which lets the sender know whether the message was understood correctly.

text: Which part of speech is the word 'quickly' in the sentence 'She completed the task quickly'?
explanation: 'Quickly' describes how the action 'completed' was done, so it is an adverb, since adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or other adverbs.

text: Which of the following is a good practice while listening to someone speak?
options: Interrupting frequently to share your own views
Planning your reply while the other person is still talking
Looking at your phone while nodding occasionally
explanation: Active listening requires giving full attention to the speaker without distraction, which helps in understanding the message correctly.

text: A sentence that expresses a strong emotion or feeling, such as 'What a wonderful view!', is called a/an
explanation: Exclamatory sentences express strong feelings or sudden emotion and usually end with an exclamation mark.

text: Which of the following best describes a 'barrier' caused by language differences?
explanation: Semantic barriers arise when the sender and receiver interpret words or language differently, for example due to unfamiliar vocabulary or jargon.

text: Which of the following is an example of a healthy way to manage stress?
options: Practising deep breathing or relaxation exercises
Ignoring the cause of stress completely
explanation: Relaxation techniques such as deep breathing help calm the mind and body, making them healthy strategies for managing stress.

text: Identifying your own strengths and weaknesses honestly is an example of
explanation: Self-awareness is the ability to recognise and understand one's own abilities, limitations, emotions and values.

text: In the SMART goal-setting technique, the letter 'M' stands for
explanation: In SMART goals, 'M' stands for Measurable, meaning progress towards the goal can be tracked using some measure or indicator.

text: Which of the following is the best example of self-motivation?
options: Studying only when a teacher is watching
Completing homework on time without being reminded
Doing work only for a reward every time
Waiting for others to push you to start a task
explanation: Self-motivation means driving oneself to act and complete tasks from one's own inner desire, without needing constant external pressure.

text: A good technique for effective time management is to
options: Do all tasks in the order they come to mind
Prioritise tasks based on their importance and urgency
Multitask on many things at once without a plan
explanation: Prioritising tasks by importance and urgency (for example using a to-do list) helps in using time efficiently and meeting deadlines.

text: Which of these is a common physical symptom of excessive stress?
options: Increased appetite for healthy food only
explanation: Prolonged or excessive stress often shows up as physical symptoms such as headaches, fatigue, or disturbed sleep.

text: Setting a goal such as 'I will improve my typing speed to 30 words per minute in two months' is an example of a
explanation: This goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound, making it a well-framed SMART goal.

text: Which of the following best helps in managing time effectively?
options: Making a daily or weekly schedule of tasks
Starting the most urgent task only after all others are done
Avoiding the use of any planner or calendar
Doing tasks randomly without any list
explanation: Preparing a schedule or to-do list helps allocate time appropriately to different tasks and reduces the chance of missing deadlines.

text: Recognising a personal weakness, such as difficulty speaking in public, is the first step towards
explanation: Awareness of one's weaknesses allows a person to take deliberate steps, such as practice or training, to improve in that area.

text: Which of the following is an example of an input device on a computer?
explanation: A keyboard is used to enter data and commands into the computer, making it an input device, while a monitor, printer and speaker are output devices.

text: Which of these is a basic file operation performed on a computer?
explanation: Renaming, copying, moving, and deleting files are common file operations carried out through a file manager or operating system.

text: Which of the following is a good practice for computer care and maintenance?
options: Keeping the computer in a dusty, humid place
Regularly cleaning the keyboard, screen and vents
Eating and drinking directly over the keyboard
explanation: Regular cleaning of computer components and keeping them free of dust helps prevent hardware issues and extends the life of the device.

text: A strong password for computer security should ideally
options: Be your name or date of birth
Be short and easy for anyone to guess
Combine letters, numbers and special characters
explanation: A strong password uses a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters, making it harder for others to guess or crack.

text: Which of the following is considered a threat to computer privacy and security?
options: Clicking on links in unknown suspicious emails
Logging out after using a shared computer
explanation: Clicking unknown or suspicious links can install malware or lead to phishing attacks, compromising the security and privacy of data.

text: Which key combination is commonly used to copy a selected file or text in most operating systems?
explanation: Ctrl + C is the common shortcut for copying selected content; Ctrl + V pastes it, Ctrl + X cuts it, and Ctrl + Z undoes an action.

text: Backing up important files regularly is useful mainly because it
options: Increases the speed of the computer
Protects data from being lost due to hardware failure or accidental deletion
Reduces the need for antivirus software
explanation: A backup is a copy of data kept separately so that it can be restored if the original file is lost, corrupted, or accidentally deleted.

text: Which of the following actions helps protect your personal information (privacy) while using the internet?
options: Sharing your passwords with online strangers
Avoiding sharing sensitive personal details on public websites
Using the same simple password everywhere
Accepting every friend request on social media without checking
explanation: Being cautious about what personal information is shared publicly online reduces the risk of misuse of that data by others.

text: Which of the following is an example of computer hardware maintenance?
options: Deleting temporary files from the hard disk
Cleaning dust from the cooling fan and vents
explanation: Physically cleaning components like the cooling fan and vents is a hardware maintenance task that helps prevent overheating and damage.

text: An entrepreneur is best described as a person who
options: Only works for a fixed salary in a company
Identifies a business opportunity and takes the risk to start and run a venture
Avoids taking any risk in business
Never plans for the future of a business
explanation: An entrepreneur recognises an opportunity, organises resources, and takes on the risk of starting and managing a new business venture.

text: Which of the following is generally considered an important quality of a successful entrepreneur?
options: Willingness to work hard and persist despite setbacks
Complete dependence on others for every decision
explanation: Successful entrepreneurs typically show hard work, persistence, and the ability to keep going despite challenges and failures.

text: Which of these is a common myth about entrepreneurship?
options: Entrepreneurs need to plan and manage finances carefully
Only people born into rich families can become entrepreneurs
Entrepreneurship involves some level of risk
explanation: It is a common myth that only wealthy or born-privileged people can become entrepreneurs; in reality, entrepreneurship is open to anyone with the right skills, ideas and effort.

text: Entrepreneurship benefits society mainly by
options: Reducing the number of goods and services available
Creating employment opportunities and new products or services
Preventing any competition in the market
explanation: Entrepreneurs create new businesses that generate jobs, introduce innovative products/services, and contribute to overall economic growth.

text: Which of the following is a key function of an entrepreneur?
options: Organising resources such as capital, labour and materials to run the business
Refusing to innovate or try new ideas
Working in isolation without any employees or customers
explanation: Entrepreneurs must organise and coordinate various resources (money, people, materials) efficiently to establish and run their venture.

text: Choosing entrepreneurship as a career option, compared to a regular job, generally means
options: Guaranteed fixed income with no risk
Taking on business risk in return for potential independence and profit
Working fixed hours set entirely by someone else
explanation: As a career option, entrepreneurship involves accepting business risk and responsibility, with the potential reward of independence and profits.

text: 'Innovativeness' as a quality of an entrepreneur mainly refers to the ability to
options: Copy existing products exactly without changes
Come up with new ideas, products or ways of doing things
Avoid any kind of creative thinking
explanation: Innovativeness means generating new ideas or improved ways of doing things, which helps a business stand out and grow.

text: Which of the following best fits the definition of 'risk-taking' in entrepreneurship?
options: Investing time and money into a venture despite an uncertain outcome
Refusing to start any activity that has any uncertainty
Only doing work that is completely risk-free
Depending entirely on luck without any planning
explanation: Risk-taking in entrepreneurship means being willing to commit resources like time, money and effort to a venture even though the outcome is uncertain.

text: Which statement about entrepreneurship as a career is TRUE?
options: It requires no planning or effort at all
It can offer flexibility and the chance to pursue one's own business idea
It is suitable only for people who have already failed at jobs
It guarantees success within the first year always
explanation: Entrepreneurship, when pursued seriously with planning, can offer flexibility, independence and the opportunity to build one's own business idea into reality.

text: Sustainable development can best be defined as development that
options: Uses up all resources quickly for immediate benefit
Meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Focuses only on economic growth and nothing else
explanation: Sustainable development balances present needs with the responsibility of preserving resources and the environment for future generations.

text: Which of the following is an example of an individual action supporting sustainable development?
options: Switching off lights and appliances when not in use
Using single-use plastic as much as possible
Cutting down trees without planting new ones
explanation: Turning off unused lights and appliances conserves energy, which is a simple and effective way an individual can support sustainability.

text: 'Green skills' refer to skills that help a person
options: Contribute to conserving or restoring the environment and using resources sustainably
Ignore the impact of human activities on nature
explanation: Green skills are the knowledge and abilities needed to support environmentally sustainable practices, such as conserving resources and reducing waste.

text: Which of these represents the three broad pillars of sustainable development?
explanation: Sustainable development rests on three interconnected pillars: economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental protection.

text: Which of the following practices helps reduce environmental pollution at an individual level?
options: Segregating waste into recyclable and non-recyclable categories
Burning plastic waste in the open
Using excessive packaging for every product
explanation: Segregating waste allows recyclable material to be processed and reused, reducing the overall burden of waste on the environment.

text: Using public transport or carpooling instead of individual vehicles mainly helps in
options: Reducing fuel consumption and lowering carbon emissions
Having no effect on the environment
explanation: Sharing transport reduces the number of vehicles on the road, which lowers overall fuel use and the emission of pollutants.

text: Which of the following is an example of the 'Reduce' principle among the 3 Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)?
options: Throwing away a plastic bottle after a single use
Buying only what is needed and avoiding unnecessary consumption
Recycling paper into new paper products
Reusing an old jar to store items
explanation: The 'Reduce' principle focuses on minimising consumption and waste generation in the first place, such as buying only what is genuinely needed.

text: Planting trees and protecting forests mainly supports sustainable development by
options: Helping maintain the ecological balance and absorbing carbon dioxide
Reducing the oxygen available in the air
Having no impact on the environment
explanation: Trees help maintain ecological balance, prevent soil erosion, and absorb carbon dioxide, all of which support environmental sustainability.

text: As a student, which of the following is a practical way to contribute to sustainable development?
options: Leaving taps running when not in use
Encouraging responsible use of resources like water, paper and electricity in daily life
explanation: Students can contribute to sustainability by practising and promoting the responsible, efficient use of everyday resources like water, paper and electricity.

text: _____ refers to focussing human efforts for maintaining a healthy body and mind, capable of withstanding stressful situations.
explanation: Stress management is specifically about maintaining a healthy body and mind so a person can handle stressful situations effectively.

whyOthersWrong.a: Artificial Intelligence is a technology concept, not a human wellness practice.
whyOthersWrong.c: Motivation is about drive and desire to achieve goals, not about withstanding stress specifically.
whyOthersWrong.d: Emotional intelligence is about recognising and managing emotions, broader than stress handling.

text: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of stress management?
explanation: Effective stress management INCREASES efficiency and productivity, not reduces it. The other three are genuine benefits of managing stress well.

whyOthersWrong.a: Boosting immunity IS a benefit — chronic stress weakens the immune system, so managing stress helps.
whyOthersWrong.c: Improving mood IS a benefit — stress causes irritability; managing it improves emotional well-being.
whyOthersWrong.d: Preventing behavioural problems IS a benefit — unmanaged stress often leads to anxiety, aggression, etc.

text: _____ are computer programs that can damage the data and software programs or steal the information stored on a computer.
explanation: Viruses are malicious programs designed to damage data, corrupt software, or steal information by replicating and spreading through systems.

whyOthersWrong.a: Spam refers to unsolicited bulk emails, not programs that damage data.
whyOthersWrong.c: Junk mail is the same as spam — unwanted email, not malicious software.
whyOthersWrong.d: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware that initialises hardware during boot-up; it is not malicious.

text: _____ is a horizontal bar present at the bottom of the Windows 7 desktop.
explanation: The Taskbar is the horizontal bar at the bottom of the Windows desktop; it contains the Start button, pinned programs, running applications, and the system tray.

whyOthersWrong.a: Status Bar appears in individual application windows (e.g., at the bottom of Writer) to show document status, not on the desktop.
whyOthersWrong.b: Menu Bar is inside application windows showing File, Edit, View etc. menus.
whyOthersWrong.d: Recycle Bin is an icon/folder on the desktop for deleted files, not a bar.

text: State whether the following statement is a Myth or a Reality: 'Entrepreneurs are born a certain way and cannot be made.'

options.c: Reality — all entrepreneurs share the same traits

explanation: This is a Myth. Entrepreneurial skills such as risk-taking, leadership, and problem-solving can be developed through education, training, and experience. Entrepreneurs are made, not just born.

whyOthersWrong.a: Incorrect — research and experience show entrepreneurship skills can be acquired and nurtured.
whyOthersWrong.c: Incorrect — entrepreneurs come from very diverse backgrounds and have different personalities.
whyOthersWrong.d: Incorrect — good entrepreneurs do plan; this option mis-states what makes it a myth.

text: Which one of the following is NOT true for entrepreneurs?
explanation: Entrepreneurs DO create jobs — they start businesses that employ people. This statement is false, making it the answer to 'NOT true'.

whyOthersWrong.a: TRUE — entrepreneurs invest their own capital and take on financial risk.
whyOthersWrong.b: TRUE — innovation is a core characteristic of entrepreneurship.
whyOthersWrong.d: TRUE — spotting market gaps and opportunities is fundamental to entrepreneurship.

text: _____ controls all aspects of a paragraph's appearance, such as text alignment, tab stops, line spacing, and borders, and can include character formatting.
explanation: Paragraph Style in OO Writer controls all paragraph-level formatting: alignment, indents, tab stops, line spacing, borders — and can also embed character-level formatting.

whyOthersWrong.a: Page Style controls page-level settings like margins, headers/footers, and orientation — not paragraph formatting.
whyOthersWrong.b: Character Style controls only inline text formatting (font, colour, bold) within a paragraph.
whyOthersWrong.c: Cell Style is a Calc (spreadsheet) concept for formatting table cells, not Writer paragraphs.

text: How many levels of headings does Open Office Writer evaluate to build the Table of Contents?
explanation: OO Writer evaluates up to 10 levels of headings (Heading 1 through Heading 10) when generating a Table of Contents.

whyOthersWrong.a: 8 is incorrect — Writer supports more heading levels than this for the TOC.
whyOthersWrong.b: 9 is incorrect — the correct number is 10.
whyOthersWrong.d: 12 is incorrect — Writer does not evaluate 12 heading levels for the TOC by default.

text: Reema has inserted many images in a pamphlet but their size is occupying too much space. Her friend suggests reducing the image size. Which option will help her do this without losing any content of the image?
explanation: Resize scales the image to a smaller size while keeping all of its content intact. The image is simply displayed at a different size, no part of it is cropped or removed.

whyOthersWrong.a: Recolor changes the colour of the image (e.g., greyscale, sepia) — it does not change the physical size.
whyOthersWrong.b: Docking refers to attaching toolbars or panels to the screen edge, not image sizing.
whyOthersWrong.d: Rotate spins the image to a different angle but does not reduce its size.

text: Which of the following graphic filters is used to increase the contrast of an image in a document?
explanation: The Sharpen filter increases the contrast between adjacent pixels, making edges more defined and the image appear crisper/higher contrast.

whyOthersWrong.a: Smooth reduces contrast by blurring edges, making the image softer.
whyOthersWrong.c: Remove Noise reduces graininess/speckles but does not specifically increase contrast.
whyOthersWrong.d: Invert reverses all colours (creates a negative image) but does not increase contrast.

text: Which of the following is NOT used when creating a mail-merge document?
explanation: Mail merge requires: a main document (Writer), a data source (spreadsheet, database, or address book), and the merge process. Paint is a drawing/image-editing application and plays no role in mail merge.

whyOthersWrong.a: A spreadsheet (e.g., Calc) can serve as the data source for mail merge.
whyOthersWrong.b: The document (main Writer file) is the template into which data is merged.
whyOthersWrong.d: A database can serve as the data source for mail merge records.

text: Which mode is used to apply a style to many different areas of a document quickly without going back to the Styles and Formatting window in Writer?
explanation: Fill Format Mode (activated from the Styles and Formatting window) lets you click multiple text areas one after another to apply the same style repeatedly, without reopening the styles panel each time.

whyOthersWrong.a: Edit Mode is the standard document-editing state; it has no special style-painting feature.
whyOthersWrong.c: New Style Mode is for creating a brand-new style, not for applying an existing one to many areas.
whyOthersWrong.d: Update Style Mode updates the style definition to match the selected text — it is not for applying a style to many locations.

text: A colored border, with _____, appears around a cell where changes are made in a shared worksheet.

options.a: a dot in the upper left-hand corner
options.b: a dot in the lower left-hand corner
options.c: a cross in the upper left-hand corner
options.d: a cross in the upper right-hand corner

explanation: In a shared Calc worksheet, when a cell is edited, a coloured border appears around that cell with a small dot in the upper left-hand corner to mark the change.

whyOthersWrong.b: The dot appears in the upper left, not lower left.
whyOthersWrong.c: It is a dot, not a cross, and it is in the upper left corner.
whyOthersWrong.d: The marker is in the upper left, not upper right, and it is a dot not a cross.

text: _____ feature adds data arranged in a group of cells in Calc, with labels for columns and/or rows.
explanation: The Subtotal feature in Calc automatically calculates subtotals for groups of related data rows, inserting subtotal rows with the labels. It handles grouped/labelled data specifically.

whyOthersWrong.a: Average is just a mathematical function, not a grouping-and-labelling feature.
whyOthersWrong.c: Goal Seek finds the input value needed to reach a desired result — it does not group or label data.
whyOthersWrong.d: Solver optimises a value subject to constraints — it is not about grouping data with labels.

text: A _____ refers to a cell or a range of cells on a worksheet whose data values can be used in a formula.
explanation: A cell reference (like A1 or B2:D5) identifies a specific cell or range whose values are used in formulas. It tells the formula exactly where to look for data.

whyOthersWrong.a: A sheet is the entire worksheet tab, not a pointer to a specific cell/range for formula use.
whyOthersWrong.b: A cell is the physical unit, but 'cell reference' is the term for using it in a formula.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Cell data' is an informal term for the content of a cell, not the technical term used in formulas.

text: _____ feature of Calc is used to test 'what-if' questions.
explanation: The Scenario feature allows users to save different sets of input values and switch between them to see 'what-if' outcomes — e.g., best case vs worst case projections.

whyOthersWrong.a: Solver finds optimal values for a formula subject to constraints — it solves a specific target, not general what-if testing.
whyOthersWrong.b: Goal Seek works backwards from a desired result to find the required input — it is a single-variable reverse calculation, not general what-if testing.
whyOthersWrong.d: Styles are for formatting cells visually; they have no computational or what-if capability.

text: Macros are especially useful to _____ the same way over and over again.
explanation: Macros record a sequence of actions and play them back on demand, making them ideal for automating repetitive tasks that need to be performed the same way repeatedly.

whyOthersWrong.b: Macros do not reject tasks; they automate and execute them.
whyOthersWrong.c: Reporting is a separate function; macros automate actions, not create reports.
whyOthersWrong.d: Adding comments is done via Insert > Comment; macros are not designed primarily for commenting.

text: _____ feature of Calc helps to track what data was changed, when the change was made, who made the change and in which cell the change has occurred.
explanation: The Record Changes (Track Changes) feature logs every edit: what was changed, the timestamp, the author, and the cell location — essential for collaborative editing.

whyOthersWrong.b: 'Edit Record' is not a Calc feature name.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Change Record' is not the correct name of this feature in Calc.
whyOthersWrong.d: Macro automates repeated tasks; it does not track who changed what and when.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of DBMS?
explanation: Impress is the presentation software in LibreOffice/OpenOffice, similar to PowerPoint. It is not a Database Management System. PostgreSQL, SQLite, and FoxPro are all DBMS products.

whyOthersWrong.a: PostgreSQL is a powerful open-source relational DBMS.
whyOthersWrong.b: SQLite is a lightweight, serverless relational DBMS widely used in apps.
whyOthersWrong.c: FoxPro (Microsoft Visual FoxPro) is an older relational DBMS with its own database engine.

text: A _____ is an interface in a user-specified layout that lets users view, enter, and change data directly in database objects such as tables.
explanation: A Form in a DBMS is a custom-designed screen that lets users view, enter, and edit data from tables in a user-friendly layout, rather than working directly in the table grid.

whyOthersWrong.a: A frame is a page-layout element (in Writer/HTML); it is not a database data-entry interface.
whyOthersWrong.c: A relation (table) is the underlying data structure, not the user-facing entry interface.
whyOthersWrong.d: A report formats and prints data for output/presentation; it is not for entering or changing data.

text: Which of the following is the expanded form of SQL?
explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language — the standard language for creating, querying, and managing relational databases.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Systematic' is not the correct first word — it is 'Structured'.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Software' is not the correct first word.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Structural' is close but wrong — the correct term is 'Structured'.

text: _____ is usually suitable for less amount of data. (Choose: Relational database / Flat file)
explanation: A flat file (single table, no relationships) is simpler and suitable for small, non-complex datasets. Relational databases are designed for larger, structured datasets with multiple related tables.

whyOthersWrong.a: Relational databases are designed for larger, complex data with relationships between multiple tables — overkill for small amounts of data.
whyOthersWrong.c: They are not equally suitable — flat files lack the power needed for large, complex data.
whyOthersWrong.d: Both CAN work for small amounts of data, but flat files are specifically noted as better suited.

text: Binary data types in a database can be used for storing _____.
explanation: Binary (BLOB) data types store raw binary data and can hold any binary file — photos, music, videos, documents, etc. They are not limited to one file type.

whyOthersWrong.b: Integer values are stored in INT/INTEGER data types, not binary types.
whyOthersWrong.c: Binary types can store any binary content, not only images.
whyOthersWrong.d: Binary types can store any binary content, not only videos.

text: _____ clause can be used with the SELECT statement in SQL to specify which rows to retrieve from the table.
explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows in a SELECT statement — only rows that meet the specified condition are returned. Example: SELECT * FROM Books WHERE Price < 500;

whyOthersWrong.b: GROUP BY groups rows for aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, etc.); it does not filter individual rows.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'SAME' is not a valid SQL clause.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'SIMILAR' is not a standard SQL clause (SIMILAR TO exists in some databases for pattern matching, but it is not used for row selection in the same way).

text: _____ is an accessibility function which is designed for people who have vision impairment or cognitive disabilities.
explanation: Sticky Keys is an accessibility feature that helps users with motor or cognitive disabilities by allowing keyboard shortcuts (like Ctrl+Alt+Del) to be pressed one key at a time instead of simultaneously.

whyOthersWrong.a: Filter Keys ignores brief or repeated keystrokes — designed for users with tremors, not specifically vision/cognitive impairment.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Sound Key' is not a standard Windows accessibility feature.
whyOthersWrong.c: Toggle Keys plays audio cues when Caps Lock, Num Lock, or Scroll Lock is pressed — helpful for vision impairment but specifically for key state notification, not the primary answer here.

text: Networks in which certain computers have special dedicated tasks, providing services to other computers (in the network) are called _____ networks.
explanation: Client-server networks have dedicated server computers that provide services (file storage, printing, authentication) to client computers. The servers have special dedicated roles.

whyOthersWrong.a: Hierarchical describes the logical arrangement/topology of the network, not a type defined by dedicated service roles.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Dedicated server' is a term for the server machine itself, not the network type name.
whyOthersWrong.c: Peer-to-peer networks have NO dedicated servers — all computers share equally and can act as both client and server.

text: _____ provides Internet access by transmitting digital data over wires of a local telephone network.
explanation: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) transmits digital data over standard copper telephone wires, providing broadband Internet access without interfering with voice calls.

whyOthersWrong.a: HSDPA (High Speed Downlink Packet Access) is a mobile/cellular 3G wireless technology, not a telephone-wire technology.
whyOthersWrong.b: P2P (Peer-to-Peer) is a network/file-sharing model, not an internet access technology.
whyOthersWrong.d: A Modem is a device that modulates/demodulates signals — DSL also uses modem hardware, but DSL is the technology/service, making it the specific correct answer.

text: A _____ is an unplanned event that may happen all of a sudden and may lead to unwanted or unprecedented results/outcomes.
explanation: An accident is an unplanned, sudden event that leads to unexpected and often harmful outcomes. It is unintentional by definition.

whyOthersWrong.a: An emergency is a serious, urgent situation requiring immediate action — it may result FROM an accident, but is not the unplanned event itself.
whyOthersWrong.b: A hazard is a potential source of harm or danger (a condition), not the sudden event itself.
whyOthersWrong.d: An illness is a health condition that usually develops over time; it is not typically described as a sudden unplanned event.

text: A _____ worker will always perform to the best of his ability.
explanation: A happy and healthy worker has the physical well-being and positive mental state that allow them to consistently perform at their best. Health and happiness directly affect productivity and quality of work.

whyOthersWrong.a: Fast working is a style, not a condition that guarantees best-ability performance; speed without well-being can lead to errors.
whyOthersWrong.b: High education levels help but do not guarantee peak performance if the worker is unhealthy or unhappy.
whyOthersWrong.d: A stressed worker typically performs BELOW their best ability due to reduced focus, health issues, and burnout.

text: _____ is the process of emptying a place in case of an emergency or disaster.
explanation: Evacuation is the organised process of moving people out of a place (building, area) when there is an emergency or disaster, to ensure their safety.

whyOthersWrong.a: Emergency is the dangerous situation/event itself, not the process of leaving.
whyOthersWrong.b: Accident is an unplanned harmful event, not a response process.
whyOthersWrong.c: A Drill is a practice/rehearsal of an evacuation procedure, not the actual evacuation itself.

text: The filename and filename extension are separated by a _____.
explanation: A dot (period) separates the base filename from its extension. For example, in 'report.docx', the dot separates 'report' from the extension 'docx'.

whyOthersWrong.a: Dollar sign is used in some programming languages for variables, not as a filename/extension separator.
whyOthersWrong.c: Underscore is used within filenames to replace spaces, not to separate filename from extension.
whyOthersWrong.d: Hash is used in URLs/HTML for anchor links or in programming for comments; not a filename separator.

text: Which of the following type of communication involves interchanging messages only through images or pictures?
explanation: Visual communication involves conveying information through images, pictures, diagrams, charts, and other visual elements — without words.

whyOthersWrong.a: Verbal communication uses spoken or written words, not images.
whyOthersWrong.b: Gesture communication uses body movements (hands, arms), not images/pictures.
whyOthersWrong.d: Facial communication involves facial expressions to convey emotions, not pictorial messages.

text: _____ is the ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as the emotions of others.
explanation: Emotional Intelligence (EI) is the ability to identify, understand, and manage both your own emotions and the emotions of people around you — a key interpersonal skill.

whyOthersWrong.a: Self-Awareness is knowing your own strengths, weaknesses, values and feelings — it is part of EI, but does not specifically cover managing others' emotions.
whyOthersWrong.c: Stress Management focuses on techniques to reduce stress, not on recognising or managing emotions broadly.
whyOthersWrong.d: Emotional Barrier is an obstacle to communication caused by emotions (e.g., anger, fear), not a skill.

text: _____ is the driving force that pushes us to achieve our goals, feel happy, and improve our quality of life.
explanation: Self-Motivation is the internal drive or force that compels a person to pursue goals, stay positive, and continuously work towards a better quality of life — without needing external pressure.

whyOthersWrong.a: Stress Management is about coping with and reducing stress — it is a technique, not a driving force.
whyOthersWrong.b: Self-Awareness is knowing yourself; it does not actively push you towards goals.
whyOthersWrong.c: Self-Growth refers to the process of personal development and improvement, not the force that drives it.

text: Which of the following is NOT an essential quality to become a successful entrepreneur?
explanation: Being wealthy is NOT an essential quality of a successful entrepreneur. Many successful entrepreneurs started with little money; what matters is creativity, confidence, perseverance, and risk-taking ability. Wealth is often an outcome, not a prerequisite.

whyOthersWrong.a: Confidence IS essential — entrepreneurs must believe in their ideas and take bold decisions.
whyOthersWrong.b: Creativity IS essential — entrepreneurs need to generate new ideas and innovative solutions.
whyOthersWrong.c: Patience IS essential — building a business takes time; entrepreneurs must persist through setbacks.

text: In total, how many SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) were adopted by the United Nations in 2015 as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure that by 2030 all people enjoy peace and prosperity?
explanation: The United Nations adopted 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

whyOthersWrong.a: 13 is incorrect — the actual number of SDGs is 17.
whyOthersWrong.b: 11 is incorrect — 11 is not the number of SDGs.
whyOthersWrong.d: 19 is incorrect — the UN adopted exactly 17 SDGs.

text: Which of the following features allows one to apply a group of formats at the same time?
explanation: Styles in OO Writer allow you to apply a predefined group of formatting attributes (font, size, colour, spacing, etc.) to text or paragraphs all at once with a single click.

whyOthersWrong.a: Fill is used to apply background colour to cells or shapes; it does not group multiple text formats.
whyOthersWrong.c: Images are inserted objects; they are not a formatting feature.
whyOthersWrong.d: Drag and Drop is a mouse operation for moving/copying objects; it does not apply formatting.

text: In Writer, the Styles and Formatting option is available under _____ menu.
explanation: In OO Writer, Styles and Formatting (F11) is found under the Format menu. It opens the Styles and Formatting panel where you can apply, create, and modify styles.

whyOthersWrong.a: Insert menu is for inserting objects (images, tables, headers, page breaks) — not for styles.
whyOthersWrong.b: Tools menu contains macros, spelling, autocorrect, and customisation options — not styles.
whyOthersWrong.d: Window menu manages open document windows — not formatting or styles.

text: Gaurav is creating a report in Writer. The image gets embedded in his document whenever he drags and drops the image and the document size increases. Suggest a way to link the image file instead of embedding it.

options.b: Hold down the Ctrl key while dragging.
options.c: Hold down the Shift key while dragging the image.
options.d: Hold down the Ctrl and Shift key while dragging and dropping the image.

explanation: In OO Writer, holding the Ctrl key while dragging an image creates a link to the image file rather than embedding it. This keeps the document size smaller since the image is referenced, not copied.

whyOthersWrong.a: Normal drag and drop embeds the image (the default behaviour described in the question).
whyOthersWrong.c: Holding Shift while dragging does not change the embed/link behaviour in Writer.
whyOthersWrong.d: Holding both Ctrl and Shift is not required; Ctrl alone creates the link.

text: Resizing a _____ may badly affect the resolution of an image.
explanation: Raster images (JPEG, PNG, BMP) are made of fixed pixels. Enlarging them stretches those pixels, causing visible pixelation and loss of sharpness. Reducing them also permanently discards pixel data.

whyOthersWrong.a: Vector images are made of mathematical paths/shapes and can be scaled to any size without loss of quality.
whyOthersWrong.c: CAD images are typically vector-based and scale without quality loss.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Coloured image' is not a file type category — colour alone does not determine whether resizing affects quality.

text: In Writer, you can create your own template in _____ way(s).
explanation: In OO Writer you can create a template in three ways: (1) Save a document as a template via File → Templates → Save, (2) From the Template Manager, (3) By dragging a document into the templates folder.

whyOthersWrong.a: One way is too restrictive — Writer provides multiple methods to create templates.
whyOthersWrong.b: Two ways is not the complete count.
whyOthersWrong.d: Four ways overstates the number of distinct template-creation methods in OO Writer.

text: In Writer, _____ function key is used to see the databases while implementing mail merge.
explanation: Pressing F4 in OO Writer opens the Data Sources panel (database browser), which is used to view and select data sources/databases when implementing mail merge.

whyOthersWrong.a: F1 opens the Help system.
whyOthersWrong.b: F2 activates the Formula Bar (in Calc); in Writer it is used for other purposes.
whyOthersWrong.c: F3 is used to insert AutoText in Writer; it does not open the database panel.

text: While consolidating data, a cell range can be named using _____ option.
explanation: In OO Calc, the 'Define Name' option (Sheet → Named Ranges and Expressions → Define) is used to assign a name to a cell range, making it easier to reference in consolidation and formulas.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Name range' is not the exact menu option name in Calc.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Define range' is not the correct option name.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Consolidate name' is not a Calc feature — Consolidate and Define Name are separate features.

text: Kawal and his friends are working on a spreadsheet for entering data and updating records. They wish to keep a track of changes — who made the changes and what changes were done in the spreadsheet. Which option will help?
explanation: The 'Record Changes' feature in OO Calc tracks all edits: what was changed, who made the change, and when. This is found under Edit → Track Changes → Record Changes.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'View Changes' shows the recorded changes list but is not what starts the tracking — 'Record Changes' must be enabled first.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Store changes' is not the name of this Calc feature.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Track changes' is the Microsoft Excel term; the OO Calc option is called 'Record Changes'.

text: _____ is a more elaborate form of Goal Seek.
explanation: Solver is an enhanced version of Goal Seek. While Goal Seek finds the input for a single variable to reach a target, Solver can optimise a formula subject to multiple constraints across several variable cells.

whyOthersWrong.a: Database is a data-storage concept; it is not related to Goal Seek.
whyOthersWrong.b: Hyperlink is a clickable link; it has no connection to Goal Seek.
whyOthersWrong.c: Report is an output/presentation tool; it is not a what-if analysis feature.

text: Macro functions can be written to behave as regular functions by writing a/an _____.
explanation: By writing an Add-In macro in OO Basic/Calc, a user-defined macro function can be exposed as a regular spreadsheet function that can be called directly in cell formulas, just like SUM or AVERAGE.

whyOthersWrong.a: Void is used in some languages to declare a function with no return value — it is not how macros become regular Calc functions.
whyOthersWrong.b: Return is used inside a function to send back a value — it is necessary but does not by itself make the function accessible as a regular cell function.
whyOthersWrong.d: Dim is the keyword in OO Basic to declare a variable — it is not used to expose a macro as a regular cell function.

text: _____ option of Calc helps in viewing the changes made to a worksheet using original and edited worksheet.
explanation: Edit → Compare Document in OO Calc compares the current (edited) version of a spreadsheet with an original saved version and highlights the differences, helping users see what was changed.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Edit → Revise document' is not a valid Calc menu path.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Edit → Consolidate' is used to merge data from multiple ranges/sheets, not to compare edits.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Edit → Collaborate document' is not a real Calc menu option.

text: In Calc, shared workbooks allow:
explanation: In a shared Calc workbook, adding/editing text data is allowed. However, several operations are restricted in shared mode: merging cells, conditional formatting, and inserting pictures/graphs are not permitted.

whyOthersWrong.a: Merging cells is NOT allowed in shared workbooks — this is a known restriction.
whyOthersWrong.b: Conditional formatting CANNOT be applied in shared workbooks.
whyOthersWrong.c: Inserting pictures or graphs is NOT supported in shared workbook mode.

text: In OpenOffice Base, the relationship applied on the tables can be removed with the help of _____ option.
explanation: In OO Base Relationships window, right-clicking a relationship line and selecting 'Delete' removes the defined relationship between two tables.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Clear' is not the option used for removing table relationships in OO Base.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Remove' is not the label of this action in OO Base's relationship editor.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Drop' is an SQL command for deleting database objects (tables, views); it is not the UI button in OO Base's relationship view.

text: In SQL, the keyword to display records in ascending order is:
explanation: ASC is the SQL keyword used with ORDER BY to sort records in ascending order. Example: SELECT * FROM Students ORDER BY Name ASC;

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Asce' is not a valid SQL keyword — the correct abbreviation is ASC.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Incr' is not a valid SQL keyword.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'High' is not a valid SQL keyword for sorting.

text: _____ is a numeric data type which can store Yes/No type values in the form of 0 or 1 in OpenOffice Base table.
explanation: Boolean (also called Bit or Yes/No) is a data type that stores only two values: 1 (True/Yes) or 0 (False/No). In OO Base, it is listed as a numeric type and stores Yes/No values.

whyOthersWrong.b: Char stores single characters or short text strings, not Yes/No values.
whyOthersWrong.c: Binary stores raw binary data (like files/images), not Yes/No boolean values.
whyOthersWrong.d: OtherObject is a data type for storing objects/files in OO Base, not Yes/No values.

text: Which of the following statements retrieves zero or more rows from one or more database tables or database views?
explanation: The SELECT statement is SQL's Data Query Language (DQL) command. It retrieves zero or more rows matching the specified conditions from tables or views.

whyOthersWrong.a: UPDATE modifies existing records; it does not retrieve/display them.
whyOthersWrong.b: DELETE removes records from a table; it does not retrieve data.
whyOthersWrong.d: DISPLAY is not a standard SQL statement.

text: Roshni has created a table Customer in SQL and wants to store photograph images of every customer under Cust_photo field. Suggest a suitable data type.
explanation: LONGVARBINARY is the data type in OO Base / HSQLDB used to store large binary data such as photographs, audio files, and other media. It is equivalent to BLOB in other DBMS.

whyOthersWrong.a: IMAGE is a data type in some DBMS (like older SQL Server), but is not the standard in OO Base/HSQLDB.
whyOthersWrong.b: PICTURE is not a standard SQL or OO Base data type.
whyOthersWrong.d: GRAPHIC is not a standard SQL data type for storing images.

text: By default, all the fields in OpenOffice Base will have _____ datatype.
explanation: In OO Base (HSQLDB), when you create a new field in the table design view, the default data type assigned is text (varchar), which stores variable-length text strings.

whyOthersWrong.a: int (tiny) stores small integer values — it is not the default field type.
whyOthersWrong.b: Boolean stores True/False — it is not the default field type.
whyOthersWrong.d: text (char) stores fixed-length text — OO Base defaults to varchar (variable-length text), not fixed-length char.

text: A _____ is a discussion style website similar to an online personal diary, used for creating personal web pages.
explanation: A Blog (weblog) is a website that functions like an online personal diary or journal, where individuals regularly post entries (articles/opinions) and readers can comment — it is discussion-style and personal.

whyOthersWrong.a: WWW (World Wide Web) is the entire system of interlinked web pages accessible via the Internet — not a single diary-style site.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Web' is a general term for the internet/websites collectively.
whyOthersWrong.d: Chat is real-time text messaging between users — not a diary-style website for creating personal pages.

text: Natasha works as floor manager. She has been assigned a task for conducting regular _____ to ensure safety of life in case of any disaster or emergency by evacuating the place of danger.
explanation: Evacuation drills are regular practice exercises where people rehearse leaving a building safely in response to an emergency or disaster. Conducting drills ensures everyone knows what to do when a real emergency occurs.

whyOthersWrong.a: Cultural assembly is a school/community event for cultural activities — not related to safety evacuation.
whyOthersWrong.b: Open house events are for showcasing a place to visitors — not emergency preparedness.
whyOthersWrong.d: Trips and excursions are recreational/educational outings — not emergency safety procedures.

text: _____ is an accessibility feature that assists people who have difficulty using a keyboard or a mouse (or both).
explanation: Sticky Keys is a Windows accessibility feature that makes it easier for users who have difficulty pressing multiple keys simultaneously. It allows pressing modifier keys (Ctrl, Alt, Shift) one at a time instead of all together.

whyOthersWrong.b: Serial key is a product activation code, not an accessibility feature.
whyOthersWrong.c: Control key (Ctrl) is a standard keyboard key, not an accessibility feature.
whyOthersWrong.d: Toggle Keys plays audio cues for Caps/Num/Scroll Lock — it helps with visual impairment, not keyboard difficulty specifically.

text: Network in which all computers have equal status is called _____.
explanation: In a Peer-to-Peer (P2P) network, all computers have equal status — any computer can act as both a client and a server. There is no dedicated central server; resources are shared directly between peers.

whyOthersWrong.b: Central architecture has one central computer controlling all others — computers do NOT have equal status.
whyOthersWrong.c: Hierarchical architecture organises computers in a tree structure with levels of authority — not equal status.
whyOthersWrong.d: Client-server architecture has dedicated servers providing services to client computers — not equal status.

text: _____ are text files with small pieces of data — like a username and password.
explanation: Cookies are small text files stored by websites on a user's device to remember information like login credentials, preferences, and session data. They allow websites to identify returning users.

whyOthersWrong.a: Operating System is the core system software (Windows, Linux) — not a small text file storing credentials.
whyOthersWrong.b: Antivirus is security software that detects malware — not a small data file.
whyOthersWrong.d: Modem is a hardware device for internet connectivity — not a file storing data.

text: DSL stands for _____.
explanation: DSL stands for Digital Subscriber Line — a technology that provides high-speed internet access over existing copper telephone lines while allowing simultaneous voice calls.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Digital System Line' is incorrect — the second word is 'Subscriber', not 'System'.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Data Subscriber Line' is incorrect — the first word is 'Digital', not 'Data'.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Data Service Line' is incorrect — none of these words match the correct expansion.

text: The school is organizing a Career Counselling Workshop. Which of the following will be the most effective method of communication to inform all students of the school?
explanation: A Notice or Poster is a formal, one-to-many communication method that can reach all students simultaneously by being displayed on notice boards across the school. It is the most efficient method for mass communication in a school.

whyOthersWrong.a: Face-to-face informal communication is one-to-one or small group — not suitable for reaching all students at once.
whyOthersWrong.c: Phone calls are one-to-one and would require calling every student individually — time-consuming and impractical for mass notification.
whyOthersWrong.d: Meeting everyone in person would require enormous time and effort to speak to each student — not practical for school-wide announcements.

text: Which of the following is the most suitable term for the ability to regulate one's own emotions and help others also to do the same?
explanation: Managing emotions is the accurate term for the skill of regulating (controlling) one's own emotional responses and also helping others regulate theirs — a key component of emotional intelligence.

whyOthersWrong.b: Harnessing emotions means channelling emotions productively, but it does not specifically mean regulating them or helping others do so.
whyOthersWrong.c: Knowing emotions refers to identifying and recognising emotions — not regulating or managing them.
whyOthersWrong.d: Suppressing emotions means hiding or pushing down emotions — this is unhealthy and the opposite of healthy regulation.

text: Roshin studies in class X and is practising hard with a lot of sample papers to get good marks in her exams. She gets up early in the morning to study and completes her revision work. This is an example of _____.
explanation: Roshin's behaviour — waking up early, practising consistently, and working hard without anyone forcing her — is driven by an internal drive. This is self-motivation: the inner force that pushes a person to achieve their own goals.
