whyOthersWrong.a: Self-awareness is knowing your own strengths and weaknesses — Roshin is acting on them, not just knowing them.
whyOthersWrong.c: Influential motivation comes from an external person inspiring you — there is no external motivator mentioned here.
whyOthersWrong.d: Emotional intelligence is about managing emotions and understanding others — not about study habits and self-driven effort.

text: A _____ is a location where a group of files can be stored in the computer.
explanation: A Folder (also called a directory) is a container in the file system used to organise and store a group of related files together.

whyOthersWrong.b: SMPS (Switched Mode Power Supply) is a hardware component that converts and supplies power to the computer.
whyOthersWrong.c: CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) is a chip that stores BIOS settings and keeps the real-time clock.
whyOthersWrong.d: UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is a device that provides backup power during electricity outages.

text: Which of the following is a myth about entrepreneurs?

options.a: An entrepreneur should be confident and should be able to take decisions.
options.b: Every business idea must be unique or special.
options.c: An entrepreneur should keep trying new ideas.
options.d: An entrepreneur should be creative and should have different solutions to the problem.

explanation: It is a myth that every business idea must be unique or special. Many successful businesses are based on existing ideas but executed better (e.g., improved service, lower price). What matters is execution, value delivery, and market need — not absolute uniqueness.

whyOthersWrong.a: TRUE — confidence and decision-making ability are genuine qualities of successful entrepreneurs.
whyOthersWrong.c: TRUE — trying new ideas and learning from failure is a real entrepreneurial trait.
whyOthersWrong.d: TRUE — creativity and problem-solving with multiple solutions are genuine entrepreneurial qualities.

text: Which one of the following is the most important factor for sustainable development and helps us become aware of our role as a responsible citizen?
explanation: Education is the most important factor for sustainable development. It raises awareness about environmental issues, helps citizens understand their rights and responsibilities, and empowers them to make informed choices for a sustainable future.

whyOthersWrong.a: Sports promotes health and teamwork but does not primarily drive sustainable development awareness.
whyOthersWrong.c: Business can support or harm sustainability; it is not the most fundamental driver of awareness.
whyOthersWrong.d: Illiteracy is an obstacle to sustainable development, not a factor that promotes it.

text: Ravi has to prepare a project report. He wants to save certain formatting features and then apply them on the project report. He can use the _____ feature of OpenOffice Writer.
explanation: Styles in OO Writer let you save a set of formatting attributes (font, size, spacing, colour) under a named style. You can then apply that saved style to any text in one click, ensuring consistency across the document.

whyOthersWrong.b: Image is for inserting pictures — not for saving or applying text/paragraph formatting.
whyOthersWrong.c: Mail Merge is for creating personalised documents from a data source — not for saving formatting.
whyOthersWrong.d: Preview shows how the document will look when printed — it does not save or apply formatting.

text: During a recent excursion, Roshni has taken some pictures for making a report in Writer. She wants to increase the contrast of the images. Which one of the following image filters should she use in Writer?
explanation: The Sharpen filter in OO Writer increases the contrast between adjacent pixels in an image, making edges more defined and the overall image appear crisper and higher contrast.

whyOthersWrong.a: Aging gives the image an old, sepia-toned appearance — it does not increase contrast in the modern sense.
whyOthersWrong.b: Mosaic pixelates the image by averaging colour blocks — this reduces fine detail rather than increasing contrast.
whyOthersWrong.d: Smooth blurs the image by averaging nearby pixels — this reduces contrast and sharpness.

text: Which one of the following image arrangement options in Writer sends the drawing object behind the text?
explanation: The 'Behind the text' arrangement option places the image/drawing object in a layer behind the text, so text flows over the image. This is different from 'To background' which places it behind all other objects.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'To background' sends the object to the very back, behind all other drawing objects — but 'Behind the text' specifically positions it relative to text.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'To foreground' brings the object in front of everything, including text.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Back one' moves the object one layer back in the Z-order of drawing objects, but it does not specifically place it behind the text layer.

text: _____ feature of Writer is based on different types of heading styles and is used to give the listing of the contents of the document.
explanation: The Table of Contents (TOC) feature in OO Writer automatically generates a listing of the document's contents by reading the heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, etc.) and their page numbers.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Table of Heading' is not a feature name in OO Writer.
whyOthersWrong.b: Index is an alphabetical listing of terms and page numbers found at the end of a document — not the same as the Table of Contents which lists headings in document order.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Label of Contents' is not a standard OO Writer feature.

text: _____ is the default template for the files being created in Writer.
explanation: When you create a new document in OO Writer without specifying a template, it uses the 'Blank document' (default template) — an empty page with basic default settings for margins, font, and page size.

whyOthersWrong.a: Resume template is a specific pre-designed template for writing CVs — not the default.
whyOthersWrong.b: Project Report is not the default template for new Writer documents.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Chapter' is not the name of the default template in OO Writer.

text: Shanta is creating a project report in Writer and wants to apply the same style on headings/titles in the entire document as she has done at the beginning. She can use the _____ feature of Writer to apply the same format on each line/word, wherever needed.
explanation: Fill Format mode (also called Fill Format Mode) in OO Writer lets you 'paint' a style onto multiple text areas by clicking them one after another — without reopening the Styles panel between each application.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Fill Style' is not the correct name of this feature — the correct term is 'Fill Format'.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Apply Feature' is not a standard OO Writer feature name.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Apply Character' is not a Writer feature name for this purpose.

text: To add your own comments in Calc, select _____ → Track changes → Comment.
explanation: In OO Calc, comments for tracked changes are added via Edit → Track Changes → Comment. The 'Edit' menu contains the Track Changes submenu.

whyOthersWrong.a: File menu is for document operations (Open, Save, Print) — not Track Changes.
whyOthersWrong.c: Insert menu adds objects (rows, columns, images, charts) — not for Track Changes.
whyOthersWrong.d: Data menu is for data operations (Sort, Filter, Subtotals) — not for Track Changes.

text: To add a new sheet in the spreadsheet, click on the _____ sign located at the left bottom of the spreadsheet.
explanation: In OO Calc, the '+' (plus) button is located at the left bottom of the spreadsheet, next to the sheet tabs. Clicking it adds a new blank worksheet to the workbook.

whyOthersWrong.a: The asterisk (*) is used as a multiplication operator in formulas; it is not the button to add a sheet.
whyOthersWrong.b: The slash (/) is used as a division operator in formulas; it is not a sheet-adding button.
whyOthersWrong.c: The percent (%) sign is used for percentage calculations; it is not a sheet-adding button.

text: _____ is a set of values that can be used within the calculations in the spreadsheet to explore and compare various alternatives depending on changing conditions.
explanation: What-if Scenarios (Scenarios feature in Calc) lets you create named sets of input values. You can switch between scenarios to see how different values affect calculated results — ideal for exploring various alternatives.

whyOthersWrong.a: Sort rearranges existing data in ascending or descending order — it does not explore alternative input sets.
whyOthersWrong.b: Filter shows a subset of data based on criteria — it does not model alternative calculations.
whyOthersWrong.d: Comments are notes attached to cells for documentation — they have no calculation or scenario function.

text: The recorded macros are actually stored as _____.

options.a: a set of instructions in a programming language

explanation: When you record a macro in OO Calc, the actions you perform are translated into and stored as OO Basic programming code — a set of instructions in the Basic programming language that can be re-run to repeat those actions.

whyOthersWrong.b: Macros are not stored as cell sequences — they are stored as program code.
whyOthersWrong.c: Macros are stored as Basic modules within the document file, not as a standalone document.
whyOthersWrong.d: Macros are code instructions, not a list of values.

text: While creating a hyperlink in Calc, if the complete path along with filename is given, then it is an example of _____.
explanation: An Absolute hyperlink contains the full/complete path to the target file (e.g., C:\Users\Student\data\report.ods or https://www.example.com). It does not depend on the location of the current file.

whyOthersWrong.a: A Relative hyperlink contains a path relative to the current file's location — NOT the complete full path.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Mixed hyperlink' is not a standard category of hyperlink in Calc.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Folder hyperlink' is not a standard hyperlink type in Calc.

text: This tool in Calc allows you to create a group of cells automatically and apply common functions like sum, average on the grouped data. It is known as _____ tool.
explanation: The Subtotal tool in Calc (Data → Subtotals) automatically groups related rows and inserts subtotal rows between the groups, applying aggregate functions (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, etc.) to each group.

whyOthersWrong.a: Sum is a basic arithmetic function — it does not group data or manage multiple groups automatically.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Function' is a general term for all spreadsheet formulas; it does not specifically name this grouping tool.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Common' is not the name of a Calc tool.

text: _____ is the database software that is used to create, manipulate and manage data.
explanation: Ingress (or Ingres) is a relational database management system (RDBMS) used to create, store, manipulate, and manage data. Among the given options, it is the only database software.

whyOthersWrong.b: Writer is a word-processing application (like MS Word) — not database software.
whyOthersWrong.c: Paint is a basic graphics/drawing application — not database software.
whyOthersWrong.d: Windows is an operating system (platform) — not database software.

text: The process of arranging data in ascending or descending order is known as _____.
explanation: Sorting is the process of arranging records/data in a specific order — either ascending (A to Z, 1 to 9) or descending (Z to A, 9 to 1) based on one or more fields.

whyOthersWrong.a: Filtering shows only records that meet specific criteria — it does not rearrange the order of data.
whyOthersWrong.b: Tracking (Record Changes) monitors who made edits to data — not about arranging data in order.
whyOthersWrong.c: Purification is not a standard database operation term.

text: With reference to LibreOffice Base, which of the following is a valid data type to indicate the monetary values?
explanation: Currency is a valid data type in LibreOffice Base (HSQLDB) used to store monetary values. It is a fixed-point numeric type designed specifically for financial calculations with exact decimal precision.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Money' is not a standard data type in LibreOffice Base/HSQLDB (it exists in some other DBMS like SQL Server).
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Rupee' is a currency unit, not a data type name in any database system.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Dollar' is a currency unit, not a data type name in any database system.

text: Data can be retrieved and displayed from one or more tables in a DBMS using a _____.
explanation: A Query is a request/instruction to the DBMS to retrieve specific data from one or more tables. SQL SELECT statements are used to write queries. Queries can combine, filter, sort, and calculate data from multiple tables.

whyOthersWrong.a: Referential integrity is a rule that ensures foreign keys in one table match primary keys in another — it is a constraint, not a data retrieval mechanism.
whyOthersWrong.b: Domain defines the allowed set of values for a field — it is a constraint concept, not a retrieval tool.
whyOthersWrong.d: A Field is a single column in a table — it is a structural element, not a retrieval mechanism.

text: While designing a form, it is suggested to get the date input by adding the _____ to the date field to prevent entering invalid dates.
explanation: Adding a Calendar control to a date field in a LibreOffice Base form provides a date picker that displays a visual calendar. This ensures users can only select valid dates from the calendar, preventing invalid date entry.

whyOthersWrong.b: Text input allows any text to be typed freely — a user could type an invalid date like '30/02/2025'.
whyOthersWrong.c: Timer is a control for timing/countdown purposes, not for date selection.
whyOthersWrong.d: Number input accepts numeric values — a user could enter any number, which would not validate as a proper date.

text: While designing a form, titles, headings or sub-headings may be added using _____ tool available on the Form Controls tool box.
explanation: The Label control in the LibreOffice Base Form Controls toolbox is used to add static display text such as titles, headings, field descriptions, and sub-headings to a form. Label text is not editable by the user.

whyOthersWrong.a: Textbox (Text Field) is an input control where users type data — not for displaying fixed headings/titles.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Title' is not a Form Controls tool name in LibreOffice Base.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Heading' is not a Form Controls tool name in LibreOffice Base.

text: _____ is a state of physical, mental and social well-being.
explanation: Health is defined by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being — not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.

whyOthersWrong.a: Richness refers to wealth or abundance of resources — not a definition of well-being in the physical/mental/social sense.
whyOthersWrong.b: Popularity is being well-liked by others — it is a social concept, not a health definition.
whyOthersWrong.d: Activity refers to physical movement or work — it is part of a healthy lifestyle, but not the definition of health itself.

text: Which one of the following is a class B ignition material?
explanation: Class B fire hazard materials are flammable liquids and gases (petrol, diesel, LPG, natural gas, paints, solvents). Gas is a Class B ignition material. Water extinguishers must NOT be used on Class B fires.

whyOthersWrong.a: Paper is a Class A material (ordinary combustibles like wood, paper, cloth).
whyOthersWrong.c: Electrical equipment fires are Class C (energised electrical fires) — not Class B.
whyOthersWrong.d: Potassium (and other reactive metals) are Class D materials (combustible metals).

text: The _____ has prepared the policy to provide employees with a healthy and safe work environment.
explanation: DoIT (Department of Information Technology, now Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology / MeitY) is the government body responsible for IT sector policies in India, including workplace safety and health guidelines for IT sector employees.

whyOthersWrong.a: GoIT is not a recognised Indian government IT policy body.
whyOthersWrong.c: ToIT is not a recognised Indian government IT policy body.
whyOthersWrong.d: SoIT is not a recognised Indian government IT policy body.

text: RSI stands for:
explanation: RSI stands for Repetitive Strain Injury — a condition caused by repetitive movements or overuse of a body part (e.g., typing, clicking a mouse), leading to pain, numbness, or weakness in muscles, tendons, and nerves.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Recurring Syndrome Injury' is not the correct expansion.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Repetition Symptom Injury' is not the correct expansion.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Recessive Stress Injury' is not the correct expansion.

text: _____ is the science that deals with designing and arranging the things at workplace so that people can use them easily and safely.
explanation: Ergonomics is the science of designing workplaces, equipment, and tools to fit the needs of the human body, improving comfort, efficiency, and safety. For IT workplaces, this includes chair height, monitor position, keyboard angle, etc.

whyOthersWrong.a: Health science broadly covers human health — it is not specifically about designing workplace arrangements.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Fixture science' is not a recognised field of study.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Work Economics' is not the name of this discipline; the correct term is Ergonomics.

text: Which one of the following is a WRONG safety guideline?

options.a: Store all cleaning chemicals in tightly closed containers in separate cupboards.
options.b: Never distract the attention of people who are working near a fire or with some machinery, tools or equipment.
options.c: Wear loose clothing or jewellery while working with machines.
options.d: Make sure all areas have proper lighting.

explanation: Wearing loose clothing or jewellery near machinery is DANGEROUS — it can catch in moving parts and cause serious injury. The correct rule is to wear fitted clothing and remove jewellery when working with machines.

whyOthersWrong.a: Correct safety rule: chemical containers should be tightly closed and stored separately to prevent spills and reactions.
whyOthersWrong.b: Correct safety rule: distracting people near fire, machinery or tools can cause accidents.
whyOthersWrong.d: Correct safety rule: proper lighting is essential to see hazards and work safely.
